fieldMarks: Very small, slender snake, about 8-10 in (Louisiana reports 6-13 in) with smooth scales in 15 rows.
Black or dark-brown head, a light collar, then a black neck band; body light brown, tan or reddish-brown, unpatterned.
Belly white, pink or yellowish; young resemble adults; tiny eyes.
behavior: Highly fossorial; burrows under rocks, woody debris, leaf litter and in rotting logs or stumps and is rarely seen except when cover is turned.
Eats centipedes, insect larvae, earthworms, spiders, termites and snails; small rear fangs do not threaten people.
Active March to October in the north; lays 1-3 eggs under cover in summer.
habitat: Dry, well-drained wooded ridges and hillsides, pine and oak woodland, sandy pine flatwoods and sandhills, always with cover such as rocks, logs and stumps.
range: Southeastern United States from North Carolina west to Louisiana, with an isolated population in Kentucky (Indiana also records it); generally absent from southern Georgia and peninsular Florida; not in Canada.
